subject: Forecasts for an ARMA only model

messages.author: debdb86a14910224
messages.subject: Forecasts for an ARMA only model
parts:
I'm testing a simple ARMA model against a gaussian process smooth.

fit.ARMA <-
  brm(bf(DV  ~ 1),
      autocor = cor_arma(formula = ~ 1, p = 1, q = 1),
      family = student(link = "identity"),
      prior = c(set_prior("student_t(3,0,5)", class = "b"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,5)", class = "Intercept"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,1)", class = "ma"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,1)", class = "ar")),
      chains = 3,
data)

fit.GP <-
  brm(bf(activeDevices  ~ 1 + 
           s(DaysTime, k = 50, bs = "gp") +
           s(WeekDay, k = 7, bs = "gp")),
      family = student(link = "identity"),
      prior = c(set_prior("student_t(3,0,5)", class = "b"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,5)", class = "Intercept"),
                set_prior("student_t(3,0,50)", class = "sds")),
      chains = 3,
data)

I can get straightforward forecast predictions from the GP just by supplying newdata that extends the DaysTime and WeekDay variables forward a week. However, I can't seem to figure out how to correctly supply the newdata to the ARMA model to get a weekly forecast. I understand that in the ARMA model, the formula I used specifies the order of the observations as a covariate which leads me to wonder if am I missing something simple about how to supply the newdata to the predict function.

Thanks much!

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: Forecasts for an ARMA only model
parts:
The problem with brms is that it is so general that specifying forecasts for explicit time-series models (I mean those specified via argument autocor) through newdata is not trivial to implement.
In order to ARMA forecasts to make sense, we have to know the response values at those future time points to be predicted. Of course we don't know them or otherwise we wouldn't need forecasts. The canonical solution is to use the predicted values of future responses to compute further future responses, but this is not possible to specify via newdata (as least I didn't figure out yet how to do it). As a result, unfortunately and a bit embarrassingly, forecasts for structures implemented via autocor are not yet possible (it is just not the main focus of brms).

There is an open issue targeting this problem (https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/147) and I hope to provide a solution sooner rather than later.

messages.author: debdb86a14910224
messages.subject: Re: Forecasts for an ARMA only model
parts:
Ah. Thanks for the explanation Paul and the link to the github issue. While I'm at it, I should add that brms is a great general use package. I mean I did just fit a guassian process smooth and a ARMA model using it, which is frankly phenomenal. 

And please take this only as me brainstorming how to get time series forecasts out of BRMS while hopefully not burdening you. But I wonder if either Rob Hyndman (Forecast package) or Steve Scott (BSTS package) might have any interest or resources in taking on some of the development task. I know Hyndman has a generic forecast function that covers a few different models (ARMA, ets, stlf) and I know Scott's predict accepts a forecast horizon although I don't know how he manages the sampling. I'll admit though that beyond these loose associations, I'm uncertain what the development costs would be for them, for you, or if it would even work given other constraints. 

Cheers!

messages.subject: Re: Forecasts for an ARMA only model
parts:
This really is helpful brainstorming, thanks! I am not that of an expert in time-series modeling myself and some guidance will certainly help me in getting this implemented.

At the moment I am not yet sure if it is just a conceptual problem or a problem of implementation. Likely it is just a conceptual problem given that, once you have the full posterior distribution (thanks to Stan for making this possible!), nearly everything is doable in a reasonable amount of time if you just know how to correctly handle the posterior samples. Of course, I will find out whether it is an implementation problem, too, once I am working on the implementation.... ;-)
